added_lemmas.justification: The scientifically admissible priming range has a largest element, and monotonicity shows that this single maximal fiber determines range identification, strict signs, whole-set coverage, and the existence of a sign breakdown.
added_lemmas.gap: Existing vaccine challenge-effect bounds do not give the exact maximal-fiber reduction or an attained sharp breakdown point for a bounded fraction of response-altering noninfecting exposures.
added_lemmas.consumer: Trial analysts solve the model once at \(\bar\delta=\max\mathcal D\) for range identification and coverage, and solve the nested opposite-side feasibility programs over \([\delta_0,1]\) only when they need the exact breakdown threshold.

prose_updates.tldr: Changing pathogen variants make early-versus-late vaccine challenge risk depend on one latent coupling of exposures and responses across periods. The response type permits a noninfecting period-one exposure to alter later controlled susceptibility, and \(\delta\in[0,1]\) bounds the altered fraction. The compatible full-law classes, reduced fibers, and sharp ratio images are nested in \(\delta\); hence a nonempty closed sensitivity range \(\mathcal D\) is represented exactly by its largest value \(\bar\delta=\max\mathcal D\), without a continuum closure. Opposite-side linear-program feasibility defines attained sharp priming breakdown points, with dual strict-sign certificates below a finite threshold and a compatible counterlaw at it. Exact multinomial inversion, including \(\Gamma_0(0;\gamma)=\Delta\), gives unconditional whole-set coverage by projecting only through the maximal fiber. The single-variant and Perényi--Stensrud anchors are projection and calibration comparisons, not class inclusions or transfers.

project_justification.gap: Janvin and Stensrud (2025) give sharp single-pathogen challenge-effect bounds, and Perényi and Stensrud (2025, Section 5) identify a variant-specific time-to-event challenge subtype effect under their own exposure and proportionality restrictions. Those results provide projection and calibration anchors, not class inclusions. Neither supplies an exact maximal-fiber sensitivity theorem, a sharp attained priming breakdown frontier, or unconditional whole-set projection for a reference-mixture ratio built from trial first-infection risks and external exposure margins when a prior noninfecting exposure may alter later controlled susceptibility.
project_justification.niche: The target compares one policy-fixed reference mixture across periods and defines period-two challenge risk after no period-one exposure. A history-indexed response array separates that target from the response after a noninfecting exposure, while \(\delta\) restricts their disagreement without substituting selected case-strain frequencies for external exposure margins. Because the restriction weakens monotonically with \(\delta\), every scientifically justified closed range \(\mathcal D\) reduces exactly to \(\bar\delta=\max\mathcal D\); without a controlled validation substudy, \(\bar\delta=1\).
project_justification.fill: The substantive chain gives exact common-history compression, an always-defined extended sharp set, finite reciprocal endpoints under the separate denominator condition, and common-law sign duals. It now proves law-class, fiber, and ratio-image nesting, exact equality of the sensitivity-range union with the maximal fiber, attained sharp positive- and negative-side priming breakdown points, dual certificates before each finite threshold, and compatible counterlaws at the threshold. Exact primitive-cell multinomial inversion projects through the single maximal fiber for unconditional coverage of the whole sensitivity-range identified set. For \(K=2\), the Perényi--Stensrud comparison remains a positive-face projection and calibration test, not a class-inclusion result.

prose_updates.related_work: Janvin and Stensrud (2025, Theorem 1 and Appendix B) establish sharp finite single-pathogen two-period challenge-effect bounds and attaining laws. The one-variant result here is a projection and calibration check against their survivor-selection geometry; it does not assert inclusion in, or transfer to, their published class. Perényi and Stensrud (2025, Section 5 and the marginal \(CSE_k\) identification proposition) identify a time-to-event challenge subtype effect from observed cause-specific hazards under their stated time-to-event exchangeability, positivity, consistency, exposure necessity, no cross-infectivity, covariate-invariant exposure-ratio, and scaled-new-infection proportionality restrictions. Here their controlled-risk coordinates are projected onto \(\rho_{ta}(x,e^{(v)})\), and equality with their observed-hazard comparator is a calibration statement characterized by a computable quadratic cross-product on the linear-program-computed affine hull of the positive common-history face; it is not a class inclusion or transfer claim. Tomer and Biccler (2022) analyze temporal movement under specified competing-variant mechanisms. Follmann and Huang (2018), Gilbert et al. (2001), Edlefsen (2014), and van der Laan and Gilbert (2023) motivate why selected infecting strains require extra exposure and susceptibility restrictions, so case frequencies are not substituted for the external margins \(q\). Balke and Pearl (1997) inform the finite response-type lift. Romano and Shaikh (2010) and Kaido, Molinari, and Stoye (2019) inform whole-set projection; the present exact multinomial construction includes \(\Gamma_0(0;\gamma)=\Delta\), uses a union bound without block independence, and, by sensitivity nesting, projects only through \(\bar\delta=\max\mathcal D\) to cover the entire sensitivity-range identified set.
prose_updates.honest_scope: Exact common-history projection, the unconditional extended sharp set, finite attained reciprocal endpoints under the separately disclosed fiber-wide denominator condition, and common-history sign separation hold pointwise in \(\delta\). Sensitivity nesting strengthens the range report: for every nonempty closed \(\mathcal D\), the union of compatible laws and the sharp ratio set equal their counterparts at \(\bar\delta=\max\mathcal D\). A finite breakdown point is the attained first \(\delta\) at which the appropriate opposite-side linear program is feasible; feasibility at one only decides whether such a breakdown exists and does not locate an interior threshold. The target period-two risk uses \(R^{[0]}_{21v}\), whereas observed period-two infections use \(R^{[H_1]}_{2av}\); their discrepancy among noninfected exposees is bounded, not suppressed. The \(K=2\) and single-variant anchors are projection and calibration results only, with no claim of class inclusion or transfer to the Janvin--Stensrud or Perényi--Stensrud classes. Whole-set confidence coverage is unconditional over realized counts, uses no independence among sampling blocks, and reduces to projection through the maximal sensitivity fiber. External exposure margins remain primitives; pooled case-strain frequencies do not replace them.

sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The trial and exposure cell probabilities are covered by exact likelihood-ratio-ordered multinomial inversions at Bonferroni level \(\alpha/4\) for each of two arms and two periods. At total count zero, \(T_p(0)=0\) and \(\Gamma_0(0;\gamma)=\Delta\), so zero-total and zero-cell samples require no correction. For a prespecified nonempty closed \(\mathcal D\), nesting makes the sharp range set equal to \(\Theta_{I,\bar\delta}(b,q,\omega)\), where \(\bar\delta=\max\mathcal D\); the simultaneous primitive confidence set is therefore projected through each candidate's single nonempty \(\mathcal P_{\bar\delta}(b',q',\omega)\) fiber. The resulting set covers the whole sensitivity-range identified set unconditionally and does not studentize or select an endpoint optimizer.

prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The parameter \(\delta\) bounds whether a period-one exposure that did not infect changes the period-two controlled response relative to no prior exposure. Routine negative tests establish noninfection, not absence of immune priming, and serial serology need not detect response-relevant cellular or mucosal changes; neither identifies a small \(\delta\). Without a randomized or controlled validation substudy, the honest range is \(\mathcal D=[0,1]\), so identification, strict-sign, and coverage audits use the unrestricted fiber at \(\bar\delta=1\). Endpoint opposite-side feasibility decides whether a sign breakdown exists, but an interior \(\delta_\star^+\) or \(\delta_\star^-\) must be located from the nested linear-program family over \([\delta_0,1]\). The finite history map still abstracts from multiple distinct noninfecting exposures within one period.

statement_notes.gap: This is a projection and calibration comparison to Janvin and Stensrud (2025), not a novelty claim, class inclusion, or transfer result.
statement_notes.consumer: Readers can verify the new program against the established one-pathogen proof boundary without treating the two maintained law classes as nested.
